metadata.note: WEEKLY PROGRESS REEL for the clauding project, week of 2026-09-11. SECOND reel of this date — 09-11-1 covers LoonNet; this one covers a different project entirely and shares only the channel, host and chassis. THE WEEK, as reported by the author via the repository he supplied (https://github.com/nikhil-kunapareddy/clauding): he replaced a Swift/AppKit menu bar app with a Python/PyObjC one and released it as clauding 1.0.0. RAW-MATERIAL PROVENANCE — READ THIS: the author explicitly authorised the repository's own prose (the 'feat!: replace the Swift menu bar app with a Python one' commit body and CHANGELOG.md 1.0.0) as the week's raw material, in place of dictated bullets. Every narrative claim in this reel traces to one of those two documents or to a line of source verified by hand. Nothing was inferred from diffs alone. ATTRIBUTION RULE FOR THIS REEL, set by the author: NAME THE PROJECT, NOT THE PERSON. On screen and in narration the upstream is 'claude-status-bar' or 'the original'; the upstream author's name appears nowhere in narration, on-screen text, PEDAGOGY.md or SOURCES.md. This differs from 09-11-1's rule (no collaborator named at all) and from the repository's own README and ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md, which do name him — the reel is deliberately more reserved than the repo. THROUGH-LINE: the rewrite deleted more than it wrote, and the deletions are not one kind of deletion. Some things were dropped by taste; others stopped being necessary because one design decision dissolved the need for them; and one hazard was deleted rather than defended against. The reel refuses to collapse those into 'we made it leaner'. FIGURES — READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING ANY NUMBER ON SCREEN. Every figure was verified by the assistant against the cloned repository at commit 29b2269, not taken on trust: 46 files changed / 2196 insertions / 2843 deletions (git show --stat); 2285 lines removed from .swift/.js/.sh and 1873 lines of Python added (git show --numstat); 10 Python modules under src/clauding/ totalling 1873 lines (wc -l); 58 tests = 46 plain 'def test_' functions + 12 parametrised cases on test_model_label (counted in tests/test_transcript.py:40-58), which reconciles exactly with the commit body's '58 tests, replacing the 3 Node ones'; POLL_INTERVAL = 0.5 s (bar.py:47); TAIL_BYTES = 8192 (transcript.py:15); NSApplicationActivationPolicyAccessory (bar.py:229); absolute-path hook commands (install.py:37-43). NO figure appears on screen that is not in that list. No benchmark, no CPU or memory measurement, no install count, no star count, and no timing comparison against the Swift version appears anywhere, because none was supplied or measured. ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B07 and the verdict/outro only. Body beats run ChipGrid -> STILL -> DivergentFates -> BinaryBranch -> ChipGrid; no two consecutive beats share a pattern. SHORTS / 9:16: ClaudeScienceLayerStack and ClaudeScienceSourceFlow — the guide's default B01/B02 patterns — still have NO registered 916 sibling (re-verified against Root.tsx 2026-09-11) and are avoided for that reason alone. Every pattern used here has one (ClaudeComposerAsk916, ClaudeScienceChipGrid916, DivergentFates916, BinaryBranch916, ClaudeVerdictArtifact916, LogoOutro916), so shorts.py rewires with no new TSX. B02 is the only user-media beat and would otherwise be centre-cut; it carries a hand-composed pantry/B02-916.png from make_plates.py and HOLDS rather than pans. NARRATION CARRIES NO POSITIONAL REFERENCE ('top left', 'the third one') because the same mp3 plays over both the landscape and portrait plates and the row order differs. typeScale 1.4 on the two deck patterns, which were authored against a 1280x720 stage; the 916 siblings take {data} only and ignore it harmlessly. Deck-pattern strings are budgeted to the measured limits: DivergentFates startLabel <=22 ch, each note <=42 ch; BinaryBranch label <=27 ch, detail <=45 ch/line, fix <=33 ch including the arrow. Fixed-x SVG text does not reflow, so a long string overprints silently and Remotion still exits 0. OUTRO: LogoOutro, not ClaudeTitleOutro, whose handle is hardcoded to @NikBearBrown. B08 narration is 5 words so it finishes inside the 4.0s card before its fade. './art run' will print a SKIN LINT line asking for ClaudeTitleOutro; it is wrong for this channel and is expected.

beats.narration_text: This is clauding. A menu bar indicator for Claude Code, and this week I replaced the whole thing — a Swift app, rewritten in Python. This is Sai. The rewrite deleted more than it wrote. But I don't want to tell you it's leaner. I want to separate what I chose to drop from what simply stopped being necessary.

show.event: the ask types in — the week's question, not the week's summary
the three result lines land under it, the arithmetic first
the last line names the thing the rest of the reel has to earn

props.command: clauding 1.0.0 — a Swift menu bar app, rewritten in Python. 2,196 lines written, 2,843 deleted. Don't tell me it's leaner. Tell me which deletions were taste, which ones one design decision made unnecessary, and which one deleted a hazard instead of defending against it.
props.runningText: reading back what the rewrite removed…
output: no bundle · no signing · no DMG

beats.narration_text: So, what is it. A macOS menu bar indicator for Claude Code, and it tells you three things — whether Claude is working, whether it's waiting on you, and which model and effort level the session is running. That is the entire feature set. Ten modules, eighteen hundred lines of Python, fifty-eight tests. And it makes no network requests at all.

show.event: the platform and the three states land first — the whole feature set
the install path fills in, and what it refuses to ship as
the size and the test count close the grid

props.caption: A Python rewrite of claude-status-bar — same hook protocol, same state-file design

beats.narration_text: Here it is, all three. Idle — a dim spark, then the model and the effort level. Clauding — the same line, the spark now in Anthropic's orange, while a turn is running. And waiting for input, an amber dot, because that is the one that actually needs you. Notice the width barely moves between them. That is deliberate.

show.event: the three states hold together — the whole interface at once
the eye reads the two spark states first, which differ only in colour
then the dot, which is the only state that changes shape
the caption names what each state means

still.composed_from: the three state lines transcribed verbatim from the author's README.md code block and bar.py:61-63, rendered as a plate by make_plates.py at 3840x2160
still.note: HOLD, not kenburns: the point of the beat is that the three lines are nearly the same width, and a zoompan push would destroy exactly that comparison. THIS IS A RENDERING, NOT A SCREENSHOT — it is labelled as such on the plate itself, and the strings are transcribed character-for-character from README.md and from bar.py's own state table (POLL_INTERVAL block, lines 61-63). The two colours are the literal constants in bar.py:50-51 — BRAND_ORANGE (0.851, 0.467, 0.341) = #d97757 and AMBER (0.95, 0.73, 0.18). No colour was eyeballed. Portrait override at pantry/B02-916.png stacks the same three rows with more leading; shorts.py's centre cut would slice the model/effort text off the right of every row.

beats.narration_text: Now separate them. One pile went because a single design decision dissolved the need for it — a plain process can own a status item, so the app bundle, the code signing, the notarization, the disk image and the Homebrew cask all stopped existing together. The other pile I chose to drop. Animations, a timer, a sound, an update checker. That one is taste, and I should say so out loud.

show.event: one number at the start of the track — every deleted line, undifferentiated
the split opens on the only question worth asking: why did it go
the upper track climbs — things that stopped being necessary
the lower track falls, and it fell because someone decided it should

data.slideMeta: 2,843 LINES DELETED · NOT ONE KIND OF DELETION

beats.narration_text: And here is the decision I'd defend. The original had a real hazard. Hook commands went through a PATH lookup, so a binary planted in a project directory could be found first, and the installer had to harden against that. The rewrite writes an absolute path instead. No lookup happens, so there is no ordering left to get wrong.

show.event: the hook command poses the question as one fork
the hardening branch: correct, and the lookup still happens
the absolute-path branch: nothing goes looking at all
the resolver names the difference — defending a thing versus removing it

data.slideMeta: THE HOOK COMMAND · ONE HAZARD, TWO ANSWERS
data.question: Harden the PATH, or remove the lookup?

branches.label: Write an absolute path
branches.detail: name the executable; no search runs

resolver.label: Hardening defends a lookup
resolver.detail: the rewrite deleted the lookup instead — a clauding-hook planted in a project directory can never be found first, because nothing goes looking

data.ghostText: the test for it survived the rewrite, and now asserts the real hook ran

beats.narration_text: And what survived. None of the Swift did — but the behaviour did. The liveness check that asks whether the process is alive rather than timing it out. The recovery for the two cases that fire no hook at all. The eight kilobyte transcript tail, gated on modification time. Those were hard-won upstream, and I kept every one of them.

show.event: the three behavioural carry-overs land first — the subtle ones
the protocol and the format follow: the interface was never the problem
the test count and the licence close it

props.caption: A rewrite is where subtle behaviour goes to die — these were kept on purpose

beats.narration_text: So: one page. Clauding is a Python rewrite — two thousand two hundred lines written, two thousand eight hundred deleted. One design decision removed the bundle, the signing, the notarization and both distribution channels at once. Seven features went because I chose. And the PATH hazard went because the lookup did.

show.event: the page opens on the arithmetic — what was written against what was removed
the single design decision lands, with everything it took with it
the seven dropped features, named as a choice rather than a saving
the hazard line closes the page — deleted, not defended

artifactLines: clauding is a Python rewrite of claude-status-bar: 2,196 lines written against 2,843 deleted, across 46 files. 10 modules, 1,873 lines of Python, 58 tests replacing 3.
One design decision — a plain process with an accessory activation policy can own a status item — removed the .app bundle, the codesigning, the notarization, the DMG and the Homebrew cask together.

Seven features were dropped on purpose, not for size: three animation styles, the elapsed timer, the completion sound, the update checker, the thinking words, the per-session dropdown and the per-tool activity labels.

Hook commands are now absolute paths, which deletes the PATH-ordering hazard rather than defending against it. What was kept is behavioural: process liveness, interrupt recovery, and the mtime-gated tail.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you've just finished a rewrite, try this. List everything it deleted, then sort that list into two piles — what you chose to cut, and what stopped being necessary because of some other decision entirely. Count both. The second pile is the interesting one, and it is the one nobody ever puts in the release notes.

show.event: the handoff prompt types in, ready to paste
the emphasis lands on WHY each thing went, not on how much went
the ask ends on the pile that never reaches a changelog
